title: Driver station
summary: DS laptop, Ethernet vs Wi-Fi, firewall, joysticks.

start.question: What is wrong at the driver station?

options.label: DS will not connect to the robot in the pit
DS is red on the field, no FMS
Comms flicker or ping is high
Communications indicator is only half lit
Laptop is slow, sleeps, or updates
DS software will not open or shows a firewall warning

pit-link.question: How is the DS connected to the robot?

pit-ethernet.title: Ethernet in the pit
steps: Plug the cable into the radio DS port. Check link lights on the laptop and the radio.
Turn the laptop Wi-Fi off. Disable every other adapter in ncpa.cpl. Set the Ethernet adapter to DHCP.
Check the team number in the DS Setup tab.
Turn off the Windows firewall, all three profiles.
Ping 10.TE.AM.2. A reply with the DS still red means the DS software, not the network. Restart the DS.

steps.text: Is the DS still not connecting?
steps.yes: Swap the cable or use a USB Ethernet adapter.

pit-wifi.title: Wi-Fi in the pit
steps: Check whether 2.4 GHz pit Wi-Fi is on at this event. Many events turn it off.
The network name is the team number plus the suffix set at the kiosk. The password is the team's 2.4 GHz key.
Unplug Ethernet while on Wi-Fi. Two adapters on the robot network break mDNS.
Check the team number in the DS Setup tab and turn off the firewall.

steps.text: Is the DS still not connecting on Wi-Fi?
steps.yes: Use an Ethernet cable to the radio DS port.

field-ds.title: DS red on the field
steps: Check Enet Link in the Diagnostics tab. Off means the field cable or the laptop port. Reseat both ends. Try the spare cable.
Turn Wi-Fi off with the hardware switch. Disable other adapters. Set Ethernet to DHCP.
Check the team number in the Setup tab matches this match.
Turn off the Windows firewall. Run ipconfig /release and ipconfig /renew.
Close and reopen the DS software. Only one copy.

steps.text: Is the DS still red on the field?

latency.title: Comms flicker or high trip time
steps: Trip time is measured to the radio, not the roboRIO, so roboRIO CPU does not cause it.
Check the DS log for bandwidth. Over 4 Mbps means a camera stream is saturating the link and raising trip time. Lower the resolution or frame rate.
Close any dashboard, browser, or camera viewer not needed in the match.

steps.text: Does trip time drop after cutting bandwidth?

steps: The link itself is the issue. Use the Robot drops or lags guide in this app to check signal strength and the RF environment.

options.label: It does not show up in the DS at all
It shows up but the wrong buttons or axes respond
It shows up but nothing responds

laptop.title: Laptop settings for competition
steps: Set sleep to Never for plugged in and on battery. Set the power mode to Best Performance.
Pause Windows Update for the event. Do not let it install during a match.
Close everything except the DS and the dashboard. Uninstall third-party antivirus.
Bring the charger to the field and plug in at the station.

steps.text: Is the laptop still too slow to run the DS?

firewall.title: Firewall or DS software problems
steps: Open wf.msc and turn off the Domain, Private, and Public profiles.
Add rules to allow the DS and mDNS if the school locks the firewall. Otherwise use a loaner laptop.
Remove third-party antivirus that adds its own firewall.
Reinstall NI FRC Game Tools for this season if the DS will not open. Run as administrator once.

steps.text: Does the DS still fail to open or connect?

comms-half.title: Communications indicator is only half lit
steps: The Communications indicator is split into a TCP half and a UDP half. Half lit means one protocol reaches the roboRIO and the other is blocked. Usually UDP control passes and TCP or dashboard traffic is blocked.

steps.text: Are the Robot Code indicator, joysticks, and roboRIO IP all good?
steps.no: Work the roboRIO and code side first. Use the roboRIO guide.

steps: Open the DS Diagnostics tab and look at Firewall. Dom, Pub, or Prv lit in orange means a firewall is on.
Turn off any enabled firewall. A firewall blocking one protocol is the usual cause of a half lit indicator.

steps.text: Is the Communications indicator full green now?

steps: Reseat the Ethernet cable at both the roboRIO and the radio, then restart the robot code from the Diagnostics tab.

joystick-missing.title: Controller does not show up in the Driver Station
steps: Press F1 in the DS to rescan. Every controller in the USB tab should be green.
Unplug and replug it. Use a port on the laptop rather than a hub, and a powered hub if a hub is unavoidable.
Open Windows Device Manager and look for the controller while you unplug and replug it.

steps.text: Does it appear in Device Manager at all?
steps.no: The laptop is not seeing it. Swap the cable, then the controller.

steps.text: Does it show in Device Manager with a warning triangle?
steps.yes: Update or reinstall the driver, then replug it.

steps: Restart the Driver Station software. F1 rescans at any time, enabled or disabled.

steps.text: Is it still missing from the DS?
steps.yes: Swap the controller. Worn cables drop under vibration.

joystick-mapping.title: Wrong buttons or axes respond
steps: Look at the switch on the back of a Logitech F310. X is XInput, D is DirectInput, and they map buttons differently.
Code written with XboxController expects XInput, so the switch belongs on X. WPILib's XboxController matches the Xbox 360, Xbox One, and the F310 in XInput mode.
Unplug and replug after moving the switch so Windows enumerates it again, then press F1 in the DS.
Check the slot order in the USB tab. Drag each controller into the slot the code reads.

steps.text: Do the right buttons respond now?
steps.no: Check the port numbers in the team's code against the USB tab with them.

joystick-dead.title: Controller is listed but nothing responds
steps: Move a stick and watch the axis bars in the USB tab. No movement there means the controller, not the code.
Drag each controller into the slot the code expects. Slots reorder when one is unplugged.
Restart the Driver Station software if a controller is listed but greyed out.

steps.text: Do the axis bars move in the USB tab?
steps.yes: The controller is fine, so work the robot code with the team.

steps.text: Is it still dead after a replug and a rescan?
steps.yes: Swap the controller. Worn cables drop under vibration.
